title: Jazz Chisholm Jr.’s pain was ‘a million’ after groin strike, will continue not wearing a cup
content:
NEW YORK — Jazz Chisholm Jr. was back in the New York Yankees’ lineup Friday night after exiting Thursday’s game against the Chicago White Sox when he fouled a ball off of his groin area.

Chisholm was asked how much pain he was in when he decided to take himself out of Thursday’s game in the middle of his at-bat.

“A million,” Chisholm said. “If you ever got hit in the testicles, you’d know.”

The second baseman spent his Thursday night icing his testicles, but the Yankees’ training staff did not express concern that it would be a long-term injury after the pain subsided.

Chisholm added that he’s never worn a cup since he began playing baseball, even when they were required in the minor leagues. Before Thursday night’s incident, he never had a reason to wear one.

“I’ve never gotten hit in the balls,” Chisholm said matter-of-factly. “I’m not gonna change. That was just an unlucky instance right there.”

Yankees manager Aaron Boone said the biggest difference between this generation of MLB players from when he played is their lack of a close relationship with athletic supporters.

“I did nothing without a cup, baseball-related,” Boone said. “I think the first time I heard Adrián Beltré didn’t wear a cup at third, it blew my mind. I know a lot of these guys don’t wear cups; I don’t wear a cup anymore.

“Literally, if we were going out for team pictures and I was getting dressed, like, hold on, I gotta put my cup on. It’s different now. They’re playing on pretty nice fields.”

In 2009, Beltré took a ground ball to the testicles, causing internal bleeding. His Seattle Mariners teammate, Ken Griffey Jr., conspired with Safeco Field’s stadium operations team to change Beltré’s walk-up music in his first game back to a piece from “The Nutcracker Suite” by famed classical composer Tchaikovsky.

Chisholm felt vindicated in his decision when he learned the Hall of Fame third baseman also chose not to wear protection.

“If you don’t trust your hands, I recommend you wear a cup,” Chisholm said. “I feel like it’s more defensively that you would wear a cup than hitting. At the same time, I’ve just never thought about wearing a cup.”

Chisholm started his 2026 season slowly at the plate. He did not hit his first home run until April 23. To get out of his offensive slump, he started borrowing the pants of teammates Trent Grisham and Giancarlo Stanton, and the bats of teammates Aaron Judge and José Caballero.

He will not be asking his teammates for other baseball equipment.

“I’m not asking anyone to use anything,” Chisholm said while grinning. “I’m not wearing a cup.”

YES Network’s cameras showed the Yankees’ dugout laughing after Chisholm initially fouled the pitch off. There was also a picture of Boone at home plate checking on his star player, blowing a bubble with his hand on his hip.

“Well, there wasn’t much I was gonna do,” Boone said. “I was just kind of waiting to see if it would subside. The trainer was down there, and I didn’t want to get down there. And it was time to blow bubbles.”

Concern from his teammates grew after the second baseman left the game. But the ribbing resumed once they found out he would be fine.

“They (were) just asking me how my balls felt,” Chisholm said.
